props.gloss_en: the mishna: to where does one rescue them? -- to an alley that is not open
Ben Beteira: even to an open one
Rav Chisda: three walls and two posts -- that is an alley that is not open
Rav Chisda: three walls and one post -- that is an open alley
Rav Chisda: and both [the first tanna and Ben Beteira] are per R' Eliezer
the preparation of an alley -- Beit Shammai: a post and a beam
Beit Hillel: either a post or a beam
Rabba: two walls and two posts -- that is an alley that is not open
Rabba: two walls and one post -- that is an open alley
Rabba: and both are per R' Yehuda
R' Yehuda: one who has two houses on two sides of the public domain makes a post here and a post there, or a beam here and a beam there, and carries about in between
they said to him: one does not make an eruv for the public domain in this way
Rav Ashi: three walls and one post -- that is an alley that is not open
Rav Ashi: three walls without a post -- that is an open alley
Rav Ashi: even for R' Eliezer, who said we require [two] posts -- that is for food and drink
Rav Ashi: but for a Torah scroll, one post suffices
